review.verdict: Cast is right (human guard, two AI robots) and the riso-duotone style is consistent, but a clipped robot, a badge that blends into the human, keys that read as a claw/wrench, and a missing door/seam make the trust-at-the-threshold joke hard to parse — this needs another pass before publishing.
revisionNotes: Robot1 is clipped at the left safe-area edge (lint: x 2…338) — move it inboard to roughly x=0.16 and scale down to ~0.55 so the whole body, including the reaching arm, clears the margin.

The badge prop overlaps the human's torso in the same blue tone and doesn't read as attached to robot1's outstretched hand — reposition it to float just off robot1's right hand and outline it in r-ink for contrast.

The 'keys' raw SVG reads as a mechanical claw or wrench, not a ring of keys — simplify to a clear circular ring with 2 flat teeth and nest it directly into the human's open palm so the handoff is legible.

Brief calls for a half-open door and a soft vertical seam splitting the scene into two panels (pause vs. hand-off); neither appears — add the door behind robot1 and a faint center seam so the 'one trusted, one not' metaphor actually reads.

The filing cabinet is a tiny, cropped briefcase shape at scale 0.6 with no visible spilling papers — scale it up to ~0.9 and bring 2-3 paper shapes clearly outside its edge so FILES spilling reads as the punchline prop.

This straight row of four props split by a handoff near a cabinet is very close to the recent 'Records' piece (two robots + vertical line + cabinet); change the arrangement, e.g. cluster the cabinet behind robot2 instead of lining up all four elements.
